infraction_names: Game Play Error — Missed Trigger
Game Play Error — Game Rule Violation
scenario: Annie has a Phantasmal Bear equipped with Sword of Body and Mind for several turns. Nathan casts Unsummon, targetting the Bear. Annie calls the judge because the Bear has protection from blue. Nathan claims that Annie still must sacrifice the Bear.
ruling:
Nathan should get a warning for a GRV, since he cannot target the bear
Annie should get a warning for a Missed Trigger, since the bear's trigger is detrimental. Rewind the casting of Unsummon, but do nothing about the equipment.
policy_source: IPG/MTR (not in the Comprehensive Rules corpus)

infraction_names: Game Play Error — Game Rule Violation
scenario: Anivia casts a Hellspark Elemental and attacks. Before damage, Nidalee casts Path to Exile, targetting Hellspark Elemental. Anivia puts the Elemental into her graveyard. She passes the turn. Nidalee untaps, draws a card, plays an Island and passes the turn. Anivia untaps and draws, at which piont Nidalee remembers that the Elemental should be in exile, not in the graveyard. She calls a judge.
ruling: Both players get a warning for a GRV. Nidalee because it was her spell which resolved incorrectly and Anivia for moving the Elemental to the wrong zone. This is one of the partial fixes listed in the IPG, just put the Elemental into the correct zone and continue.
policy_source: IPG/MTR (not in the Comprehensive Rules corpus)

infraction_names: Tournament Error — Communication Policy Violation
scenario:
The graveyards contain Shatter, Evolving Wilds, Accorders' Shield and Noble Hierarch.

Alice attacks with her Tarmogoyf. Natalie asks ``how big is your Tarmogoyf" and Alice says ``it's a 3/4". Natalie blocks with both Runeclaw Bear and the players put one of the Bears and the Tarmogoyf into the graveyard. At this point Sally stops the match and calls a judge to point out that the Tarmogoyf is  a 4/5 and shouldn't have died.
ruling: Alice gets a warning for a CPV because the mis-communication affected the game state. The size of the Tarmogoyf is Derived Information and she gave an incorrect answer. CPVs are something which we can back up for and here it's clear to back up to before blockers. Return the creatures to the battlefield and let  Natalie block with the correct knowledge of the size of the Tarmogoyf.
policy_source: IPG/MTR (not in the Comprehensive Rules corpus)

infraction_names: Game Play Error — Game Rule Violation
Game Play Error — Failure to Maintain Game State
scenario: At the end of Adam�s turn, Nolan casts Enlightened Tutor, searches for a card and places it on top of his library forgetting to reveal it. On Nolan�s turn,  he draws his card and Adam realizes that Nolan did not reveal properly for Enlightened Tutor and calls a judge. Nolan currently has 3 cards in hand and shows the judge an Island, a Runeclaw Bear and a Sylvan Library.
ruling: Nolan receives a Game Rule Violation Warning. Adam receives a Failure to Maintain Game State Warning. Leave the game state as it is. Since Adam had the chance to correct the error while the card was still uniquely identifiable on top of the library this is not Hidden Card Error. If Nolan shortcutted the procedure and moved the card directly to his hand such that Adam had no chance to fix the problem instead issue Nolan a Hidden Card Error Warning. Have Nolan reveal his hand to Adam who selects a card. If it's not an enchantment then shuffle it away and Nolan correctly resolves the Enlightened Tutor.
policy_source: IPG/MTR (not in the Comprehensive Rules corpus)

infraction_names: Game Play Error — Game Rule Violation
Game Play Error — Failure to Maintain Game State
scenario: Antony controls a Rhox Maulers with no counters on it and Nathan controls no creatures. Antony attacks Nathan with the Rhox. Nathan declares no blocks. Antony says "Renown trigger" and taps the Rhox as they record the combat damage. Antony then casts a Vastwood Gorger after combat and passes the turn,  forgetting to add counters to the Rhox Maulers.
ruling: Antony receives a Game Rule Violation warning and Nathan receives a Failure to Maintain Game State warning. Make it clear to Nathan that once Antony has explicitly called out the trigger it is both players' responsibility to resolve it correctly. infraction_names: Game Play Error — Hidden Card Error
scenario: Aliona casts Nissa's Pilgrimage. She has two instant/sorcery cards in her graveyard. She searches her library for three Forests, puts one into play but the  other two directly into hand without revealing them. Nicole calls a judge because Aliona didn't reveal the cards which went to hand.
ruling: Aliona receives a Hidden Card Error Warning. Aliona reveals her hand to Nicole who selects two cards in Aliona's hand. Each one of those which is a Forest remains in Aliona's hand. Each one which is not gets shuffled back into Aliona's library. Aliona searches for that number of additional Forests and puts them into her hand.

infraction_names: No infraction
scenario:
Akash controls a Gideon, Ally of Zendikar. He says "zero Gideon" and doesn't adjust the die, but also doesn't put a token into play. He then goes to attacks and attacks with Gideon, at which point Nelson calls a judge, being confused about what's going on.

Nelson isn't cheating - he just assumed that Akash was going to get tokens out later. Akash thought that the 0 ability was the one that turned it into a creature (like all the other Gideons).
ruling: No infraction has been committed, just a confusion about the actions taken. Akash has made it clear what his intention was by attacking. Rewind the game to the point that Gideon's +1 ability is on the stack (in case Nelson wants to respond) and increase the loyalty counter on Gideon.
policy_source: IPG/MTR (not in the Comprehensive Rules corpus)

infraction_names: Game Play Error — Game Rule Violation
scenario: AJ controls no non-land permanents, but does have an awakened land from casting Clutch of Currents last turn. He casts Ugin's Insight and thinking that it   checks power, rather than converted mana cost, scrys 3 (putting one on the bottom) before drawing three cards. At this point Nora notices what's going on, points out that AJ should not have scryed at all and calls for a judge.
ruling: Because AJ scried (the error) before the action which could not be publically correctable, this is not HCE. AJ receives a warning for a Game Rule Violation. Shuffle away any scried cards which are not in hand into the random portion of the library, then put three cards at random back on top and correctly resolve Ugin's Insight

infraction_names: Game Play Error — Game Rule Violation
Game Play Error — Failure to Maintain Game State
scenario: Anita casts Vastwood Gorger and passes. Nimmel casts Clutch of Currents for its awaken cost, awakening one of his tapped lands and passes. Anita casts Vastwood Gorger again and passes, Nimmel draws and plays a land, then casts Roil Spout, again for its awaken cost, awakening the same (tapped) land. When  resolving Roil Spout, Nimmel changes the die on the land from 3 to 4. Anita draws and casts Vastwood Gorger and passes. Nimmel untaps, draws and attacks with the awakened land. Anita blocks with Vastwood Gorger at which point Nimmel realises that the land should be a 7/7 and Anita calls for a judge.
ruling: Nimmel receives a warning for Game Rule VIolation. Anita receives a warning for Failure to Maintain Game State. Rewind the game to the point that Nimmel incorrectly updated the die (which will involve a random card from both players to rewind each draw, and undoing the casting of the Vastwood Gorger). If you do not back up then leave the game state as is. Do not just adjust the die from 4 to 7 since Anita has made decisions based on the current value. You may also want to investigate both players for cheating.
policy_source: IPG/MTR (not in the Comprehensive Rules corpus)

infraction_names: Game Play Error — Looking at Extra Cards
scenario: Adam has a Calculated Dismissal and two other instant/sorcery cards in his graveyard. He casts a Screeching Skaab then picks up the top 3 cards of his library in one go and drops them into his graveyard, before realizing that he has too many cards (it should be 2) and calling a judge
ruling: Adam receives a Looking at Extra Cards Warning. The judge should ask Adam whether or not any of the cards in the library are known (it's likely because of the Calculated Dismissal that the bottom card(s) may be known). Shuffle the extra card into the random portion of the library, leaving any cards which have been scried.
policy_source: IPG/MTR (not in the Comprehensive Rules corpus)

infraction_names: No infraction
scenario: Anton attacks with Mist Intruder. After damage he points at Nadine and says "Exile". Nadine hears "You go", untaps and draws. At this point Anton says "Hey wait, I said  'exile'" and calls for a judge. Anton has more actions to take post-combat.
ruling: No infraction has been committed, just a misunderstanding in the state of the game. Normally you would just rewind to the point that the disagreement occurred. However, here that would involve putting a random card from Nadine's hand on top of the library and then exile it. Do not do this. Instead get permission for a deviation, set aside a random card from Nadine's hand to be their draw for the turn. Resolve the Mist Intruder trigger with the next card in the library then when the turn is correctly passed Nadine draws the previously set aside card instead of drawing from the library.
policy_source: IPG/MTR (not in the Comprehensive Rules corpus)

infraction_names: Tournament Error — Deck Problem
Tournament Error — Decklist Problem
scenario: A player calls you over after round one. They aren't sure if they registered their deck correctly - they made a last minute change. It turns out that they have a Surgical Extraction on the list but their are actually playing a Yixlid Jailor
ruling: It doesn't matter what they played round one (whether they boarded them in or not), we don't penalise round one. However, they did register a legal list, we can't let them just change. But on the other hand, they could just play the list they intended to then get a gameloss and we'll change the list to match. We should offer them the choice to play what they registered, or take a GL to play what's in their hand.
policy_source: IPG/MTR (not in the Comprehensive Rules corpus)

infraction_names: Tournament Error — Deck Problem
scenario:
Aston plays Pacifism on Nunes' creature. Two turns later, he draws another Pacifism and calls for the judge, because he only has one Pacifism in the pool

The Pacifism in play is actually from Nunes' deck (it was shuffled in after being on Aston's creature in game 1). It has a slightly different sleeve, so they are distiguishable, but Aston didn't notice it in his opening hand.
ruling: Aston receives a game loss for Deck Problem. The penalty is an upgrade because there were more copies of a main-deck card being played than registered. Nunes receives a warning for Deck Problem.
policy_source: IPG/MTR (not in the Comprehensive Rules corpus)

infraction_names: Game Play Error — Hidden Card Error
Game Play Error — Game Rule Violation
Game Play Error — Failure to Maintain Game State
scenario:
Norton activated Griselbrand last turn, paying 7 life and drawing 7 cards. He played a spell, then passed to Ansel. Ansel draws for the turn, then the players remember that Ansel has a Spirit of the Labyrinth in play.

Norton can't remember if he asked "draw 7" or "pay 7". Ansel acknowledged whatever was asked, but doesn't remember what.
ruling:
Because Ansel controls the effect (Spirit of the Labyrinth) which changes the rules to prevent Norton from drawing, this is a warning for GRV to both players (regardless of what was or was not confirmed).

You should rewind here because the disruption to the game of letting Norton have 7 extra cards well outweighs having to rewind through Ansels' draw or potentially putting random cards back from Norton's hand.
policy_source: IPG/MTR (not in the Comprehensive Rules corpus)

scenario: Angel resolves a Time Twister, picks up her graveyard and sideboard and shuffles them together with their hand. Ned says "um, isn't that your library?"
ruling: Warning - Deck Problem. Find all the registered sideboard cards from the shuffled together pile, then random cards to make it up to 15. Return the remaining (all main-deck) cards and shuffle it into the library.

infraction_names: Game Play Error — Game Rule Violation
scenario: Nathan controls Kalitas. Artem attacks with all his creatures. Nathan blocks one of them, which is put into the graveyard, no zombie is created. Artem plays another creature post-combat and passes the turn. Artem untaps and draws, then notices that he should have a zombie.
ruling: Warning - GRV. We can't partial fix this - only the zone-change is partial fixable, not getting a zombie. We can and should rewind though. GRV to both players (it's Artem's action, but Nathan's static ability which is causing this to happen)
policy_source: IPG/MTR (not in the Comprehensive Rules corpus)

infraction_names: Game Play Error — Missed Trigger
scenario: Antoine has a Lich's Mirror in play and last turn cast a Slaughter Pact. Antoine draws for the turn, without acknowledging his pact trigger. Norman calls the judge while Antione is thinking what to play in his main phase.
ruling:
Default Action triggers are no longer specially handled. Offer Norman the choice of whether to put the trigger on the stack now. Norman will choose not to put it on the stack, since he can destroy the mirror and kill Antoine when he untaps.

Give Antoine a missed trigger warning since Slaughter Pact's trigger is Generally Detrimental.
policy_source: IPG/MTR (not in the Comprehensive Rules corpus)
